domain_symbols.random_variable: random variable on the probability space

rules.name: Nonnegativity of probability
preconditions: A is an event in the active probability space
rules.operation: Use the nonnegativity axiom of probability.
examples: Probabilities cannot be negative
counterexamples: Assigning probability -0.2 to an event is invalid

rules.name: Normalization of sample space
rules.operation: Assign total probability 1 to the whole sample space.
examples: The whole sample space has probability 1
counterexamples: Assigning total probability different from 1 violates the axioms

rules.name: Complement rule
rules.operation: Use complementarity to move between an event and its complement.
examples: If P(A) = 0.3, then P(A^c) = 0.7
counterexamples: Setting P(A^c) = P(A) in general is invalid

rules.name: Addition rule for two events
rules.operation: Correct overlap when combining probabilities of two events.
examples: Disjoint events simplify to P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B)
counterexamples: Adding probabilities without subtracting overlap is invalid when events overlap

rules.name: Conditional probability definition
rules.operation: Define conditional probability by restriction to the conditioning event.
examples: Conditional probability rescales to the event B as the new context
counterexamples: Conditioning on an event of probability 0 is invalid in this elementary rule set

rules.name: Independence product rule
rules.operation: Multiply event probabilities when independence is established.
examples: Independent coin flips multiply probabilities
counterexamples: Using the product rule for dependent events is invalid

rules.name: Law of total probability
preconditions: B1,...,Bn form a partition of the sample space
rules.operation: Expand event probability across a partition of mutually exclusive exhaustive cases.
examples: Total probability combines conditional branches over a partition
counterexamples: Using overlapping branch events as if they were a partition is invalid

rules.name: Bayes rule
rules.operation: Reverse a conditional probability using prior and evidence terms.
examples: Bayes rule reverses a conditional probability using prior and evidence terms
counterexamples: Swapping conditionals without the Bayes factor is invalid

rules.name: Linearity of expectation
rules.operation: Distribute expectation over addition and scalar multiplication.
examples: Expectation is linear even when X and Y are dependent
counterexamples: Requiring independence for linearity of expectation is invalid

rules.name: Variance definition
rules.operation: Define variance through the mean-centered square.
examples: Constant random variables have variance 0
counterexamples: Replacing centered square by E[X]^2 in general is invalid

rules.name: Covariance bilinearity seed
rules.operation: Use the centered-product definition and additive distribution laws of covariance.
examples: Covariance distributes over addition in each argument when moments exist
counterexamples: Treating covariance as multiplicative is invalid

rules.name: Bernoulli distribution rule
rules.operation: Specify the support and mass function of a Bernoulli random variable.
examples: A single biased coin flip is Bernoulli(p)
counterexamples: Assigning support outside {0,1} is invalid for a Bernoulli variable

rules.name: Binomial distribution rule
preconditions: Trials are independent and identically distributed Bernoulli trials
rules.operation: Use the binomial mass function to count successes across independent Bernoulli trials.
examples: Counting successes in n independent Bernoulli trials yields a binomial distribution
counterexamples: Using the binomial pmf when trials are not independent and identically distributed is invalid in this basic form

rules.name: Normal standardization rule
rules.operation: Center and scale a normal variable to obtain a standard normal one.
examples: Centering and scaling a normal variable produces N(0,1)
counterexamples: Dividing by variance instead of standard deviation is invalid

rules.name: Weak law of large numbers pattern
rules.output_form: convergence in probability to common expectation
preconditions: The standard iid integrability assumptions hold
rules.operation: Recognize convergence in probability of sample averages under weak-law assumptions.
examples: Repeated fair-coin averages stabilize near 1/2 in probability
counterexamples: Claiming exact equality for every finite sample size is invalid

rules.name: Central limit theorem pattern
preconditions: The standard iid finite-variance assumptions hold
rules.operation: Recognize asymptotic normality of standardized iid sums under clt assumptions.
examples: Sums of many iid bounded variables become approximately normal after centering and scaling
counterexamples: Treating the clt as an exact finite-sample identity is invalid

rules.name: Poisson distribution rule
rules.operation: Use the Poisson mass function for count variables on the nonnegative integers.
examples: Rare-event counts over a fixed interval are modeled by Poisson laws in standard settings
counterexamples: Assigning support to negative integers is invalid for a Poisson variable

rules.name: Geometric distribution rule
rules.operation: Use the geometric mass function for the waiting time to first success.
examples: Waiting time until first success in repeated independent trials is geometric
counterexamples: Using the geometric pmf when the success probability changes between trials is invalid in this basic form

rules.name: Exponential distribution density rule
rules.output_form: density lambda e^(-lambda x) on x >= 0
rules.operation: Use the exponential density for nonnegative waiting-time variables.
examples: Continuous waiting-time models with rate lambda use the exponential density
counterexamples: Extending the density to negative x in the standard exponential family is invalid

rules.name: Gamma distribution generalization rule
rules.output_form: density proportional to x^(alpha-1)e^(-beta x) on x > 0
rules.operation: Use the gamma family as a positive-support continuous distribution that contains the exponential case.
examples: Exponential waiting times sit inside the gamma family as a one-parameter slice
counterexamples: Treating gamma densities as supported on the whole real line is invalid

rules.name: Multivariate normal linear-image rule
rules.input_form: multivariate normal vector and linear map
preconditions: The random vector is multivariate normal
rules.operation: Preserve normality under marginals and linear transformations in the multivariate normal family.
examples: Any fixed linear combination of jointly normal coordinates is normally distributed
counterexamples: Applying the rule to arbitrary non-normal vectors is invalid

rules.name: Correlation normalization rule
rules.operation: Normalize covariance into a dimensionless correlation coefficient.
examples: Correlation rescales covariance to a dimensionless quantity between -1 and 1 in the standard setting
counterexamples: Dividing covariance by Var(X)+Var(Y) is invalid

rules.name: Tower property of conditional expectation
rules.operation: Average a conditional expectation back to the original expectation.
examples: Conditioning and then averaging back over the coarser information returns the original expectation
counterexamples: Dropping integrability requirements from conditional expectation arguments is invalid

rules.name: Law of total variance
rules.operation: Decompose total variance into conditional and between-condition contributions.
examples: Total variance splits uncertainty into within-condition and between-condition components
counterexamples: Replacing the sum by a product is invalid

rules.name: Almost-sure convergence implies convergence in probability
rules.input_form: X_n converges almost surely to X
rules.output_form: X_n converges in probability to X
preconditions: All random variables are defined on the same probability space
rules.operation: Pass from almost-sure convergence to the weaker convergence-in-probability mode.
examples: Stronger pointwise probabilistic convergence implies the weaker in-probability mode
counterexamples: Reversing the implication in general is invalid

rules.name: L2 convergence implies convergence in probability
rules.output_form: X_n converges in probability to X
rules.operation: Pass from mean-square convergence to convergence in probability.
examples: Mean-square convergence is stronger than convergence in probability
counterexamples: Assuming convergence in probability automatically gives L2 convergence is invalid in general
